news.headline: Young chipped in 17 points (4-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 8-9 FT), 12 assists and two steals across 35 minutes during Tuesday's 131-116 loss to Boston.
news.story: Young attempted fewer than 10 field goals despite playing 35 minutes, and he's been shifting into more of a playmaking role than a scoring one, as he's attempted 10 or fewer shots in five of his last six appearances. With Anthony Davis, Kyshawn George and AJ Dybantsa capable of handling considerable scoring responsibilities, Young doesn't necessarily need to deliver explosive scoring performances to remain an elite source of fantasy production in assists. He's averaged 15.4 points, 8.4 assists, 2.2 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game since the beginning of November.

news.headline: Young accumulated 11 points (3-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, 11 assists and one steal across 28 minutes during Sunday's 116-96 win over Orlando.
news.story: Young has shot just 26 percent over his last five games, averaging 31 minutes. However, he's recorded at least eight assists in four of those contests, maintaining fantasy value through playmaking. His shooting struggles remain concerning, but his established offensive role provides upside.

news.headline: Porter won't play Saturday against the Wizards as he's still in the process of getting up to speed on his conditioning.
news.story: Porter signed with the Magic on Nov. 25, so it's understandable that he'll need some time to get into playing shape. His next chance to play will come Sunday at Detroit on the second leg of a back-to-back set.

news.headline: Porter is signing a two-year contract with the Magic, Shams Charania of ESPN reports Wednesday.
news.story: Porter was waived by the Bucks following the preseason, though he's now set to provide backcourt depth for the Magic. He could challenge Jevon Carter for minutes behind Jalen Suggs right away. Over 38 regular-season appearances (36 starts) for Milwaukee last season, Porter averaged 17.4 points, 7.4 assists, 5.2 rebounds and 2.2 steals in 33.2 minutes per showing.

news.headline: Porter was waived by the Bucks on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
news.story: Porter will need to search for an opportunity elsewhere after failing to secure a place on the regular-season roster. He averaged 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 7.4 assists and 2.2 steals in 38 regular-season appearances a year ago with Milwaukee.

news.headline: Hield posted nine points (3-7 FG, 3-6 3Pt), four rebounds, four assists and one steal over 27 minutes during Wednesday's 107-105 win over the Hornets.
news.story: Hield has started three consecutive games, suggesting his role in Chicago's rotation is expanding. His perimeter shooting provides considerable scoring upside, but limited contributions outside three-pointers make his fantasy production susceptible to fluctuations in shot volume.

news.headline: Hield finished Sunday's 151-145 overtime loss to Denver with 33 points (13-19 FG, 7-13 3Pt), seven rebounds, six assists and one steal in 40 minutes.
news.story: Hield has averaged 16.2 points, 4.0 rebounds, 2.4 assists, 4.0 triples and 24.2 minutes over his last five games. Sunday's offensive explosion highlights his shooting upside, though inconsistent playing time limits his reliability in standard fantasy formats.

news.headline: Hield will start Sunday's game against Denver.
news.story: Norman Powell (hamstring) is sidelined, so Hield will make his first start of the 2026-27 campaign. The 2016 No. 6 overall pick started three games for the Warriors in 2025-26, averaging 9.3 points, 5.3 rebounds and 2.0 assists while shooting 40.0 percent from deep in 22.7 minutes per outing in those games.

news.headline: Clowney recorded 17 points (7-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt), five rebounds, one assist and one steal in 27 minutes during Wednesday's 104-97 victory over the Bucks.
news.story: Clowney has knocked down six triples over his last two appearances, showing improved perimeter efficiency after a scoreless outing Friday. His bench role limits his fantasy ceiling, but consistent playing time and three-point volume offer value in deeper formats.

news.headline: Clowney ended with 13 points (4-8 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one block in 26 minutes during Monday's 142-116 loss to the Timberwolves.
news.story: Clowney bounced back after going scoreless Friday against Orlando, but his production remains inconsistent. He's averaging just 5.4 points and 3.4 rebounds over his last five appearances, limiting his appeal outside deeper fantasy leagues despite his three-point upside.

news.headline: Zubac tallied 14 points (6-13 FG, 2-2 FT), 15 rebounds and one assist in 26 minutes during Monday's 125-120 victory over Oklahoma City.
news.story: Zubac tied his season high in rebounds Monday and helped Indiana snap a four-game losing streak. The big man went through a brief rough patch earlier in the month when he totaled 12 points and eight rebounds across two appearances, though he's responded well by delivering three straight double-doubles.

news.headline: Zubac notched 10 points (5-11 FG), 14 rebounds and one assist across 31 minutes during Sunday's 113-106 loss to the Knicks.
news.story: Zubac delivered a dependable performance on both ends of the court and notched his second straight double-double, marking the fourth in his last six appearances. His consistent interior role gives him a clear path to production through rebounds and efficient scoring, as he's averaging 12.5 points and 9.5 boards per game while shooting 55.9 percent from the field in that six-game span.

signals.detail: Despite the scoring inconsistency, his established starting role and contributions in assists and triples sustain his fantasy value.

news.headline: VanVleet logged six points (2-6 FG, 2-6 3Pt), two rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 31 minutes during Monday's 116-104 win over the Clippers.
news.story: VanVleet has averaged 14.2 points, 5.6 assists and 2.6 three-pointers in 30.2 minutes over his last five appearances. Despite the scoring inconsistency, his established starting role and contributions in assists and triples sustain his fantasy value.

news.headline: VanVleet contributed 25 points (10-21 FG, 3-9 3Pt, 2-5 FT), one rebound, nine assists and one steal in 33 minutes during Friday's 133-124 loss to the Nuggets.
news.story: VanVleet posted a season high in scoring and nearly finished with a double-double. He also banked in a 51-foot three-pointer at the final buzzer, though it came far too late to matter. The veteran point guard has steadily found his rhythm over the past week.

news.headline: VanVleet finished Wednesday's 119-104 victory over Indiana with 15 points (6-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt), six assists, two rebounds and one steal over 27 minutes.
news.story: It was a solid bounce-back performance for VanVleet after the veteran point guard posted only eight points during Monday's loss to the Heat. He has recorded at least six assists in two of his last three outings and six times this season. VanVleet is averaging 14.0 points, 4.9 assists, 2.5 rebounds, 3.1 threes and 0.8 steals over 29.2 minutes per game in November.

news.headline: Flagg recorded 34 points (13-27 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 7-8 FT), seven rebounds, eight assists, five steals and four blocks across 42 minutes in Friday's 113-109 win over the Suns.
news.story: Flagg filled the stat sheet in Friday's win in a way no player in NBA history had before, becoming the first player to post this kind of stat line since these five categories became official. Flagg's play down the stretch was pivotal for a Dallas team that outscored the Suns 31-14 in the fourth quarter to clinch a 25-point comeback win. As for Flagg, this was the fifth time he surpassed the 30-point mark this season, and the four blocks were a season-high output as well. news.headline: Mara (leg) is out for Saturday's game versus the Bucks, per Clemente Almanza of USA Today.
news.story: The Thunder remain pretty quiet regarding the recovery of Mara, who's facing a fourth straight absence with a shin contusion. Alex Caruso stands out as a strong streaming option in most fantasy formats while Mara is sidelined.

news.headline: Mara (leg) is out for Wednesday's game versus the Timberwolves.
news.story: This will be Mara's third straight game on the inactive list, and for now, he should be considered questionable at best for Saturday's game in Milwaukee. With Jaylin Williams (back) also unavailable, Micah Peavy and Kenrich Williams will help back up Isaiah Hartenstein at the center position.

news.headline: Mara (shin) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pacers.
news.story: Mara will miss a second consecutive contest due to a right shin contusion, with his next opportunity to play coming against Minnesota on Wednesday. With the rookie big man sidelined, Kenrich Williams and Micah Peavy are candidates for increased playing time.

news.headline: Irving (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Suns, Noah Weber of TheSmokingCuban.com reports.
news.story: The Mavericks will give Irving a breather to manage his surgically repaired left knee. His absence will likely open up more playmaking opportunities for Cooper Flagg; meanwhile, Max Christie and Naji Marshall are likely to receive a bump in playing time.

news.headline: Irving is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Suns due to left knee injury management.
news.story: Dallas could be exercising caution with Irving's surgically repaired knee. If he sits, Cooper Flagg should shoulder additional playmaking responsibilities, while Max Christie and Naji Marshall could see increased offensive opportunities. Irving's status warrants monitoring before tipoff.

news.headline: Irving contributed 11 points (5-19 FG, 1-8 3Pt), six assists, five rebounds, one block and one steal across 34 minutes during Tuesday's 120-101 win over the Nuggets.
news.story: Irving struggled mightily with efficiency but was still productive as a facilitator, finishing second on the Mavericks in assists while committing only one turnover. The veteran floor general has dished out at least five dimes in four of his last five games, averaging 20.6 points, 5.6 assists, 4.8 rebounds and 1.4 steals across 32.4 minutes per contest during that time.

news.headline: Acuff supplied 22 points (9-24 FG, 3-12 3Pt, 1-2 FT), four rebounds and nine assists over 37 minutes during Wednesday's 129-110 loss to Golden State.
news.story: The rookie guard just missed recording his fifth double-double of the season. Acuff continues to benefit from big shot volume, and through 12 games in November he's scored more than 20 points nine times, averaging 23.5 points, 7.8 assists, 3.3 boards, 2.8 threes and 0.9 steals despite shooting just 40.5 percent from the floor and 31.2 percent from three-point range.

news.headline: Acuff notched 12 points (5-14 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and four assists across 33 minutes during Monday's 123-107 loss to the Spurs.
news.story: Acuff experienced a considerable drop in production compared to Saturday's win over Boston, when he finished with 21 points, six rebounds and eight assists in 40 minutes. The rookie attempted nine fewer shots Monday and failed to connect from beyond the arc, as he had a hard time dealing with the Spurs' defensive scheme. This was the third time Acuff failed to reach the 20-point mark in his last six games, and he might be hitting a rookie wall after a hot start to the season. Some inconsistency is to be expected from a first-year guard carrying substantial offensive responsibilities, but Acuff

news.headline: Clingan totaled 10 points (3-9 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 3-3 FT), 12 rebounds, two assists and three blocks in 31 minutes during Friday's 116-94 win over Golden State.
news.story: Clingan controlled the paint again, adding another double-double and three blocks. The center is averaging 11.1 rebounds and is also shooting 41.5 percent from beyond the arc, a rare weapon for a big man. Free throws are still a weak spot at 56.3 percent, but he went perfect from the line in Friday's win

news.headline: Clingan notched five points (2-5 FG, 1-2 FT), eight rebounds, two assists and one block in 21 minutes before fouling out of Wednesday's 116-111 win over the Spurs.
news.story: Clingan's foul trouble interrupted an impressive stretch in which he averaged 14.0 points, 14.0 rebounds and 3.8 assists over his previous four games. His rebounding upside remains strong, though avoiding fouls will be important for maintaining consistent minutes.

news.headline: Clingan ended with 15 points (7-8 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 0-2 FT), 18 rebounds, five assists and two blocks in 29 minutes during Monday's 128-111 victory over the 76ers.
news.story: Clingan has recorded four consecutive double-doubles, averaging 14.0 points, 14.0 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 28.9 minutes during that stretch. His consistent rebounding, improved offensive efficiency and shot-blocking make him a strong fantasy option across all formats.

news.headline: Lendeborg finished with 18 points (5-14 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 7-9 FT), seven rebounds, two assists, a steal and two blocks across 30 minutes in Friday's 116-94 loss to the Trail Blazers.
news.story: With Stephen Curry (abdomen) and Jimmy Butler (knee) out, the Warriors have relied on Lendeborg to deliver the goods offensively, and he's posted solid numbers across the board more often than not. This was Lendeborg's best scoring performance since Nov. 16, when he had 28 points in a loss to the Pelicans, and it was also the 12th time in 19 games he's scored more than 15 points. The former Michigan standout should remain a key offensive contributor for Golden State, especially given how depleted the team is right now.

news.headline: Lendeborg supplied 15 points (6-11 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), eight rebounds, two assists, one block and three steals over 31 minutes during Wednesday's 129-110 win over the Kings.
news.story: The rookie continues to shine, with the four combined steals and blocks being his best mark since Nov. 5. Through 12 games on the month, Lendeborg is averaging 18.6 points, 7.2 boards, 3.7 assists, 1.8 threes, 1.3 steals and 0.9 blocks, failing to score in double digits just once in that span.

news.headline: Lendeborg (illness) is available for Wednesday's game against the Kings, Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
news.story: Lendeborg was questionable to suit up due to an illness, but he went through pregame warmups and will give it a go versus Sacramento. Across 17 regular-season outings (all starts), he's averaging 19.2 points, 7.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 1.0 steals, 0.8 blocks and 1.9 three-pointers in 31.8 minutes.

news.headline: Gobert ended Wednesday's 113-106 victory over the Thunder with nine points (4-6 FG, 1-6 FT), seven rebounds and one steal across 32 minutes.
news.story: Gobert was efficient, but struggled again at the free-throw line, a problem that has followed him all season. The center is still averaging double-digit rebounds, and Minnesota has learned to live with his shaky foul shooting because of what he brings defensively.

news.headline: Gobert accumulated seven points (2-2 FG, 3-4 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists, three blocks and one steal over 32 minutes during Saturday's 104-95 victory over the Grizzlies.
news.story: Gobert started to turn things around Saturday, blocking at least three shots for just the second time this season. It's been a rough season for the veteran big man, with Gobert averaging 7.6 points, 10.9 rebounds and 1.1 blocks while shooting 47.8 percent from the field and 46.2 percent from the line. However, it does appear as though his role is safe, which provides fantasy managers with a relatively safe floor, assuming blocks and rebounds are high on the priority list.

news.headline: Gobert posted nine points (4-6 FG, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds and two steals over 35 minutes during Thursday's 102-99 loss to the Knicks.
news.story: Gobert has grabbed seven or fewer rebounds in three of his last four games, an unusual slump for the veteran center. His 35-minute workload is encouraging, but inconsistent rebounding and shot-blocking have diminished his fantasy impact.

news.headline: Brown totaled 21 points (7-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal across 25 minutes during Friday's 124-100 loss to the Raptors.
news.story: Brown not only posted the best scoring output of his young career in the NBA, but he was extremely efficient for a player who has struggled with his shooting percentage in his first taste of NBA action. Brown should remain the Nets' starting point guard as long as he stays healthy. In three starts, he's averaging 14.7 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.0 steals per game while shooting 47 percent from three-point range.

news.headline: Brown finished Monday's 142-116 loss to the Timberwolves with 17 points (6-12 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, seven assists and one steal over 29 minutes.
news.story: Brown made his first career start with Nolan Traore (hamstring) sidelined. The rookie has scored at least 15 points in three straight games and could gain considerable fantasy value if he maintains a starting role, though turnovers remain a concern.

news.headline: Brown will start Monday's game against the Timberwolves, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
news.story: Brown has scored 15 and 18 points in his previous two showings, earning him the opportunity to join the starting five for the first time in his young NBA career. Coach Jordi Fernandez noted that Brown has been given the green light to log starter minutes, which would seemingly indicate that he'll sit around the 25-to-30-minute range Monday, though more clarity on his workload will be gleaned from how much he plays against the Timberwolves.

news.headline: Burries logged 23 points (9-17 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one steal over 28 minutes during Friday's 113-98 loss to the Pistons.
news.story: Burries posted his third tally of least 20 points in his past six appearances, continuing to make a case as a must-roster player. While there have been some duds sprinkled in, Burries has mostly found his rhythm in recent times, putting up top-100 value over the past two weeks. In seven games during that span, he has averaged 16.1 points, 6.6 rebounds, 2.9 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.7 three-pointers in 26.8 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Burries amassed 14 points (4-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 10 rebounds, four assists, one block and three steals across 29 minutes during Monday's 116-111 win over the Raptors.
news.story: Burries was Milwaukee's most productive reserve and finished with a game-high plus-20 rating, providing an impressive display of his all-around potential. The rookie played seven more minutes than starting guard Ryan Rollins, and Burries' ability to contribute without needing considerable shot volume should help him carve out a meaningful role alongside Tyler Herro. Burries is worth monitoring in deeper fantasy formats, particularly if he continues receiving close to 30 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Williams amassed 13 points (4-8 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, one assist and three steals in 25 minutes during Wednesday's 113-106 loss to the Timberwolves.
news.story: Williams followed his season-best scoring game Monday at Indiana with another productive night off the bench. He also tied his season high in steals. The veteran forward has quietly been one of the Thunder's most accurate three-point shooters, connecting at better than 40 percent. Oklahoma City's injuries have opened more minutes for him, and he's taking advantage.

news.headline: Williams finished with 20 points (8-13 FG, 4-6 3Pt), nine rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 26 minutes during Monday's 125-120 loss to Indiana.
news.story: Williams dropped a season-high 20 points, while also falling just one rebound short of what would have been his first double-double of the season. A plethora of injuries in Oklahoma City have presented Williams with an unexpected opportunity. While his numbers don't jump off the page, he is doing enough to be considered, even in standard leagues. In eight appearances over the past two weeks, he is averaging 10.0 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 1.5 three-pointers, good enough for top-90 value during that span.

news.headline: James (back injury management) won't be available for Saturday's game against the Rockets, according to Kris Rhim of ESPN.
news.story: James will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set after impressing in Friday's win over the Pacers, tallying 21 points (8-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, six assists and a block over 27 minutes. Dean Wade (hamstring) is questionable, while Joel Embiid (foot) and Jaylen Brown (hamstring) are out, so the 76ers will be depleted Saturday. Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe will have bigger roles on offense, while Jabari Walker, Dominick Barlow and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope will all see more minutes with James on the shelf.

news.headline: James collected 21 points (8-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, six assists and a block over 27 minutes during Friday's 111-87 win over the Pacers.
news.story: The future Hall of Famer is still averaging a career-low 17.4 points per game for the season, but he has now tallied at least 21 points in each of his last five games and remains a consistent producer across the board to the tune of 6.9 rebounds and 6.8 assists per game.

news.headline: James ended with 25 points (9-15 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), 10 rebounds, 12 assists and one steal across 35 minutes in Wednesday's 111-104 win over Miami.
news.story: With Joel Embiid (illness) ruled out and Jaylen Brown (hamstring) exiting the game, James took over. He finished with his 126th career triple-double and first as a member of the 76ers. The 41-year-old is now averaging 17.1 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.9 assists and 1.1 steals over 32.7 minutes per contest in 15 regular-season appearances in 2026-27. James isn't nearly as productive as he once was, though he should remain a reliable contributor for Philadelphia, assuming he stays off the injury report.

news.headline: Carter provided nine points (3-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 13 rebounds, three steals and two assists across 38 minutes during Tuesday's 104-86 loss to Detroit.
news.story: Carter narrowly missed out on a double-double, though his 13 rebounds led all players and matched his season-best mark. Tuesday's effort snapped a six-game stretch in which the big man recorded single-digit rebounds. On the year, Carter is averaging 12.5 points, 8.8 rebounds and 1.4 assists through 17 appearances.

news.headline: Carter amassed 15 points (5-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and one block in 32 minutes during Wednesday's 121-116 loss to Philadelphia.

The big man went through a brief rough patch earlier in the month when he totaled 12 points and eight rebounds across two appearances, though he's responded well by delivering three straight double-doubles.

news.headline: Zubac notched 10 points (5-11 FG), 14 rebounds and one assist across 31 minutes during Sunday's 113-106 loss to the Knicks.
news.story: Zubac delivered a dependable performance on both ends of the court and notched his second straight double-double, marking the fourth in his last six appearances. His consistent interior role gives him a clear path to production through rebounds and efficient scoring, as he's averaging 12.5 points and 9.5 boards per game while shooting 55.9 percent from the field in that six-game span.

news.headline: Clowney recorded 17 points (7-13 FG, 3-7 3Pt), five rebounds, one assist and one steal in 27 minutes during Wednesday's 104-97 victory over the Bucks.
news.story: Clowney has knocked down six triples over his last two appearances, showing improved perimeter efficiency after a scoreless outing Friday. His bench role limits his fantasy ceiling, but consistent playing time and three-point volume offer value in deeper formats.

news.headline: Clowney ended with 13 points (4-8 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one block in 26 minutes during Monday's 142-116 loss to the Timberwolves.
news.story: Clowney bounced back after going scoreless Friday against Orlando, but his production remains inconsistent. He's averaging just 5.4 points and 3.4 rebounds over his last five appearances, limiting his appeal outside deeper fantasy leagues despite his three-point upside.

news.headline: Gobert ended Wednesday's 113-106 victory over the Thunder with nine points (4-6 FG, 1-6 FT), seven rebounds and one steal across 32 minutes.
news.story: Gobert was efficient, but struggled again at the free-throw line, a problem that has followed him all season. The center is still averaging double-digit rebounds, and Minnesota has learned to live with his shaky foul shooting because of what he brings defensively.

news.headline: Gobert accumulated seven points (2-2 FG, 3-4 FT), 11 rebounds, two assists, three blocks and one steal over 32 minutes during Saturday's 104-95 victory over the Grizzlies.
news.story: Gobert started to turn things around Saturday, blocking at least three shots for just the second time this season. It's been a rough season for the veteran big man, with Gobert averaging 7.6 points, 10.9 rebounds and 1.1 blocks while shooting 47.8 percent from the field and 46.2 percent from the line. However, it does appear as though his role is safe, which provides fantasy managers with a relatively safe floor, assuming blocks and rebounds are high on the priority list.

news.headline: Gobert posted nine points (4-6 FG, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds and two steals over 35 minutes during Thursday's 102-99 loss to the Knicks.
news.story: Gobert has grabbed seven or fewer rebounds in three of his last four games, an unusual slump for the veteran center. His 35-minute workload is encouraging, but inconsistent rebounding and shot-blocking have diminished his fantasy impact.

news.headline: Young chipped in 17 points (4-9 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 8-9 FT), 12 assists and two steals across 35 minutes during Tuesday's 131-116 loss to Boston.
news.story: Young attempted fewer than 10 field goals despite playing 35 minutes, and he's been shifting into more of a playmaking role than a scoring one, as he's attempted 10 or fewer shots in five of his last six appearances. With Anthony Davis, Kyshawn George and AJ Dybantsa capable of handling considerable scoring responsibilities, Young doesn't necessarily need to deliver explosive scoring performances to remain an elite source of fantasy production in assists. He's averaged 15.4 points, 8.4 assists, 2.2 rebounds and 1.5 steals per game since the beginning of November.

news.headline: Young accumulated 11 points (3-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, 11 assists and one steal across 28 minutes during Sunday's 116-96 win over Orlando.
news.story: Young has shot just 26 percent over his last five games, averaging 31 minutes. However, he's recorded at least eight assists in four of those contests, maintaining fantasy value through playmaking. His shooting struggles remain concerning, but his established offensive role provides upside.

news.headline: Lendeborg finished with 18 points (5-14 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 7-9 FT), seven rebounds, two assists, a steal and two blocks across 30 minutes in Friday's 116-94 loss to the Trail Blazers.
news.story: With Stephen Curry (abdomen) and Jimmy Butler (knee) out, the Warriors have relied on Lendeborg to deliver the goods offensively, and he's posted solid numbers across the board more often than not. This was Lendeborg's best scoring performance since Nov. 16, when he had 28 points in a loss to the Pelicans, and it was also the 12th time in 19 games he's scored more than 15 points. The former Michigan standout should remain a key offensive contributor for Golden State, especially given how depleted the team is right now.

news.headline: Lendeborg supplied 15 points (6-11 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 3-4 FT), eight rebounds, two assists, one block and three steals over 31 minutes during Wednesday's 129-110 win over the Kings.
news.story: The rookie continues to shine, with the four combined steals and blocks being his best mark since Nov. 5. Through 12 games on the month, Lendeborg is averaging 18.6 points, 7.2 boards, 3.7 assists, 1.8 threes, 1.3 steals and 0.9 blocks, failing to score in double digits just once in that span.

news.headline: Lendeborg (illness) is available for Wednesday's game against the Kings, Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
news.story: Lendeborg was questionable to suit up due to an illness, but he went through pregame warmups and will give it a go versus Sacramento. Across 17 regular-season outings (all starts), he's averaging 19.2 points, 7.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 1.0 steals, 0.8 blocks and 1.9 three-pointers in 31.8 minutes.

news.headline: Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
news.story: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence, and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

news.headline: Karabell's notebook: Gobert's slow start, Zion's steals, and five other nuggets
news.story: Part of the reason I invested in Minnesota Timberwolves C Rudy Gobert in a longtime dynasty league -- and this year in a shallower format -- was so that I would not have to deal with uncertainty. Gobert is 34 years old and has been doing the same thing statistically for more than a decade. He rebounds, blocks shots and converts the field goals he attempts, and few are consistently better at this. You don't draft Gobert for assists or free throw shooting. You know what you're getting. news.headline: Morant has been diagnosed with a Grade 2 left hamstring strain and is expected to miss four weeks, Portland announced Friday.
news.story: Morant left Thursday's game early with a hamstring injury, which has since been revealed to be a strain that will result in a month-long absence. The star guard leaves a major void in the Trail Blazers' starting backcourt, one that figures to be filled by Jrue Holiday for the foreseeable future.

news.headline: James (back injury management) won't be available for Saturday's game against the Rockets, according to Kris Rhim of ESPN.
news.story: James will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set after impressing in Friday's win over the Pacers, tallying 21 points (8-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, six assists and a block over 27 minutes. Dean Wade (hamstring) is questionable, while Joel Embiid (foot) and Jaylen Brown (hamstring) are out, so the 76ers will be depleted Saturday. Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe will have bigger roles on offense, while Jabari Walker, Dominick Barlow and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope will all see more minutes with James on the shelf.

news.headline: James collected 21 points (8-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, six assists and a block over 27 minutes during Friday's 111-87 win over the Pacers.
news.story: The future Hall of Famer is still averaging a career-low 17.4 points per game for the season, but he has now tallied at least 21 points in each of his last five games and remains a consistent producer across the board to the tune of 6.9 rebounds and 6.8 assists per game.

news.headline: James ended with 25 points (9-15 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), 10 rebounds, 12 assists and one steal across 35 minutes in Wednesday's 111-104 win over Miami.
news.story: With Joel Embiid (illness) ruled out and Jaylen Brown (hamstring) exiting the game, James took over. He finished with his 126th career triple-double and first as a member of the 76ers. The 41-year-old is now averaging 17.1 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.9 assists and 1.1 steals over 32.7 minutes per contest in 15 regular-season appearances in 2026-27. James isn't nearly as productive as he once was, though he should remain a reliable contributor for Philadelphia, assuming he stays off the injury report.

news.headline: Sengun racked up 23 points (9-17 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-6 FT), 11 rebounds and 11 assists across 32 minutes during Wednesday's 116-104 win over Phoenix.
news.story: Sengun has recorded two triple-doubles in his last three appearances, reinforcing his elite fantasy upside as Houston's offensive hub. His playmaking responsibilities and consistent involvement in the paint provide multiple avenues to production, even alongside Kevin Durant.

news.headline: Sengun totaled 20 points (7-11 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-7 FT), eight rebounds, seven assists and two blocks in 31 minutes during Monday's 116-104 victory over the Clippers.
news.story: Sengun came within two rebounds and three assists of recording a triple-double, though his five turnovers were the main blemish on an otherwise impressive performance. The return of Fred VanVleet to the starting lineup didn't prevent Sengun from leading Houston in assists, highlighting how integral the Turkish big man remains to the Rockets' offensive scheme. Sengun's ability to generate playmaking production as a center continues to separate him from most players at his position in fantasy, and the two blocks were a welcome bonus. He's one of the most complete big men in the NBA, and the numb

news.headline: Sengun produced 28 points (9-16 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 9-13 FT), 11 rebounds, 10 assists, one block and one steal over 36 minutes during Friday's 133-124 loss to the Nuggets.
news.story: Sengun bounced back from an abbreviated outing in Indiana with a triple-double, tying his season high in assists. The center is averaging 21.6 points, 9.3 rebounds and 7.0 assists through 15 games.

news.headline: Simons recorded three points (1-3 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 1-2 FT) in 18 minutes during Monday's 128-111 loss to Portland.
news.story: Simons had scored 18 points in consecutive appearances before Monday's dud. He's averaging 12.0 points and 1.8 three-pointers in 24.6 minutes over his last five games, but his fluctuating workload makes him difficult to trust in standard leagues.

news.headline: Simons racked up 18 points (6-13 FG, 4-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT) and one assist in 26 minutes off the bench during Saturday's 132-129 win over the Bucks.
news.story: After starting his first game of the season Wednesday while Tyrese Maxey dealt with a minor foot injury, Simons shifted back to the second unit and delivered at least 12 points for the fifth time in the last six games. The 27-year-old guard appears to be finding a groove with his new team after signing a two-year deal with the Sixers in July, averaging 15.2 points, 2.8 threes, 1.5 boards and 1.2 assists in 24.3 minutes while shooting 44.7 percent (17-for-38) from beyond the arc.

news.headline: Simons is not in the 76ers' starting lineup against the Bucks on Saturday, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
news.story: Tyrese Maxey (foot) has been cleared to return from a one-game absence, so Simons -- who made his first start of the season Wednesday against the Magic -- will revert to the bench for Saturday's contest. Simons has averaged 14.6 points per game while connecting on 56.9 percent of his field-goal attempts over his last five outings, and although he's back to a reserve role, he should still see plenty of opportunities on offense in the continued absence of Jaylen Brown (hamstring).

news.headline: Ingram recorded 15 points (6-15 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), five rebounds, three assists and three steals in 32 minutes during Friday's 105-104 loss to New Orleans.
news.story: Ingram is still finding his rhythm three games into his return from offseason heel surgery, and his shot hasn't come around yet. He has barely connected from three since returning, but he's made his presence felt defensively. The Clippers acquired the forward from Toronto in the Kawhi Leonard trade, and they'll need his offense to climb out of the Western Conference cellar.

news.headline: Ingram registered 18 points (6-19 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), five rebounds and four assists in 26 minutes during Wednesday's 115-97 loss to the Grizzlies.
news.story: Ingram struggled with his shooting touch again, but that's to be expected after missing the first 15 regular-season outings. In his two games since returning from a partially torn Achilles, Ingram is averaging 17.0 points, 6.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists in 26.5 minutes while shooting 32.4 percent (12-37 FG) from the field and 16.7 percent (2-12 3Pt) from behind the arc.

news.headline: Ingram provided 16 points (6-18 FG, 0-6 3Pt, 4-5 FT), seven rebounds and four assists in 27 minutes during Monday's 116-104 loss to Houston.
news.story: Ingram made his season debut and first appearance for the Clippers after undergoing surgery on his heel and partially torn Achilles tendon. While the former All-Star struggled from the field, his 18 shot attempts were encouraging given he hadn't played since May, and that paints a clear picture of the role he'll have as he gets back into game shape. news.headline: Burries logged 23 points (9-17 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 3-3 FT), six rebounds, one assist and one steal over 28 minutes during Friday's 113-98 loss to the Pistons.
news.story: Burries posted his third tally of least 20 points in his past six appearances, continuing to make a case as a must-roster player. While there have been some duds sprinkled in, Burries has mostly found his rhythm in recent times, putting up top-100 value over the past two weeks. In seven games during that span, he has averaged 16.1 points, 6.6 rebounds, 2.9 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.7 three-pointers in 26.8 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Burries amassed 14 points (4-7 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), 10 rebounds, four assists, one block and three steals across 29 minutes during Monday's 116-111 win over the Raptors.
news.story: Burries was Milwaukee's most productive reserve and finished with a game-high plus-20 rating, providing an impressive display of his all-around potential. The rookie played seven more minutes than starting guard Ryan Rollins, and Burries' ability to contribute without needing considerable shot volume should help him carve out a meaningful role alongside Tyler Herro. Burries is worth monitoring in deeper fantasy formats, particularly if he continues receiving close to 30 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Bassey registered 12 points (6-9 FG), five rebounds and two assists across 23 minutes during Friday's 116-94 loss to Portland.
news.story: Bassey continued to make the most of his starting role, finishing efficiently around the rim. The center is shooting 67.1 percent from the field this season, and his activity in the paint has given Golden State a much-needed interior presence.

news.headline: Bassey chipped in 10 points (4-9 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, one assist and two blocks in 22 minutes during Wednesday's 129-110 win over the Kings.
news.story: Bassey has averaged 12.3 points, 9.3 rebounds and 1.3 blocks across 24.3 minutes over his last four games. Kristaps Porzingis' absence has expanded his opportunities, making him a useful short-term source of rebounds and defensive stats.

Meanwhile, 76ers fans mightily celebrated George leaving it. Was all that fair? news.headline: Fox (shin) is available to play in Friday's game against the Lakers.
news.story: Fox missed two straight games with a bruised right shin, but he's seemingly feeling well enough to return to the court Friday. The 28-year-old hasn't quite been his usual self from a scoring standpoint recently, averaging just 9.9 points in 27.2 minutes over his last 10 games.

news.headline: Fox (shin) is questionable for Friday's game against the Lakers.
news.story: Fox could miss a third straight game due to a right shin contusion. If he is unavailable, Jordan McLaughlin is expected to retain an expanded role.

news.headline: Fox (shin) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Portland, Jeff McDonald of the San Antonio Express-News reports.
news.story: Fox will miss consecutive games for the first time in 2026-27. He's dealing with a right shin contusion, and his next chance to suit up will come Friday against the Lakers. Stephon Castle will continue running the Spurs' offense while Jordan McLaughlin gets additional run in the second unit.

news.headline: Brunson produced 27 points (8-19 FG, 2-9 3Pt, 9-10 FT), three rebounds, eight assists and three steals over 40 minutes during Friday's 108-105 loss to the Heat.
news.story: Although Brunson missed a clutch free throw that could've changed the game in the dying moments of the fourth quarter, he still led the Knicks in scoring and was the only New York player to reach the 20-point mark. Brunson's consistency has been outstanding, as he's now scored at least 20 points in all but one of his last 12 appearances while reaching the 25-point threshold eight times.

news.headline: Brunson finished with 19 points (6-22 FG, 2-8 3Pt, 5-6 FT), three rebounds and five assists over 36 minutes during Wednesday's 121-102 victory over the Cavaliers.
news.story: Brunson had his worst shooting night of the season, but the Knicks didn't need him to be at his best. He still found ways to contribute as a playmaker, and the Knicks kept their winning streak going. With OG Anunoby (calf) out, he remains the clear focal point of a team that has climbed to 12-6.

news.headline: Brunson (illness) is available for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers, Ian Begley of SportsNet New York reports.
news.story: Brunson popped on the injury report due to an illness but will avoid his first absence of the 2026-27 campaign. In two meetings with Cleveland this season, the 30-year-old is averaging 29.0 points, 4.5 rebounds and 7.0 assists while shooting 40.0 percent from deep over 34.5 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Williams amassed 13 points (4-8 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, one assist and three steals in 25 minutes during Wednesday's 113-106 loss to the Timberwolves.
news.story: Williams followed his season-best scoring game Monday at Indiana with another productive night off the bench. He also tied his season high in steals. The veteran forward has quietly been one of the Thunder's most accurate three-point shooters, connecting at better than 40 percent. Oklahoma City's injuries have opened more minutes for him, and he's taking advantage.

news.headline: Williams finished with 20 points (8-13 FG, 4-6 3Pt), nine rebounds, two assists, one block and one steal across 26 minutes during Monday's 125-120 loss to Indiana.
news.story: Williams dropped a season-high 20 points, while also falling just one rebound short of what would have been his first double-double of the season. A plethora of injuries in Oklahoma City have presented Williams with an unexpected opportunity. While his numbers don't jump off the page, he is doing enough to be considered, even in standard leagues. In eight appearances over the past two weeks, he is averaging 10.0 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 1.5 three-pointers, good enough for top-90 value during that span.

news.headline: Brown totaled 21 points (7-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal across 25 minutes during Friday's 124-100 loss to the Raptors.
news.story: Brown not only posted the best scoring output of his young career in the NBA, but he was extremely efficient for a player who has struggled with his shooting percentage in his first taste of NBA action. Brown should remain the Nets' starting point guard as long as he stays healthy. In three starts, he's averaging 14.7 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.0 steals per game while shooting 47 percent from three-point range.

news.headline: Brown finished Monday's 142-116 loss to the Timberwolves with 17 points (6-12 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, seven assists and one steal over 29 minutes.
news.story: Brown made his first career start with Nolan Traore (hamstring) sidelined. The rookie has scored at least 15 points in three straight games and could gain considerable fantasy value if he maintains a starting role, though turnovers remain a concern.

news.headline: Brown will start Monday's game against the Timberwolves, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
news.story: Brown has scored 15 and 18 points in his previous two showings, earning him the opportunity to join the starting five for the first time in his young NBA career. Coach Jordi Fernandez noted that Brown has been given the green light to log starter minutes, which would seemingly indicate that he'll sit around the 25-to-30-minute range Monday, though more clarity on his workload will be gleaned from how much he plays against the Timberwolves.

news.headline: George logged eight points (3-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and two steals over 29 minutes during Friday's 87-86 loss to Atlanta.
news.story: George has been one of the nice surprises of the 2026-27 NBA season, but the veteran forward was not at his best Friday. He failed to score in double digits for the third time in November and was responsible for six of Boston's 26 turnovers. George is averaging 18.8 points, 5.1 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 2.0 steals and 3.5 threes over 30.1 minutes per game this month, but he figures to sit out for one leg of the Celtics' upcoming back-to-back set against the Spurs and Mavericks on Sunday and Monday, respectively.

news.headline: George closed Tuesday's 131-116 victory over the Wizards with 28 points (11-20 FG, 6-9 3Pt), four rebounds, nine assists and one steal in 33 minutes.
news.story: George's offensive efficiency was a welcome sight after he converted just six of his 21 field-goal attempts against Sacramento on Saturday. The veteran forward also led Boston in assists Tuesday while committing just one turnover. Having Jayson Tatum alongside him doesn't necessarily diminish George's fantasy appeal, particularly if he continues to embrace his responsibilities as a secondary playmaker. His ability to combine high-volume perimeter shooting with meaningful assist production makes him particularly valuable in category leagues, but he's also been a solid contributor in standard fo

news.headline: Reed posted 14 points (5-8 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds, one assist, one block and two steals in 23 minutes during Friday's 113-98 win over the Bucks.
news.story: Reed continues to produce on both ends of the floor, ensuring his spot in standard leagues is safe, at least for now. The eventual return of Jalen Duren from a hamstring injury is going to shake things up when it comes to the backup center position. While it could be argued that Reed has outplayed John Collins, it does feel as though Collins' role is a little safer at this point. With that said, managers should feel comfortable holding Reed for the time being, with a re-evaluation period likely coming in the next week or so.

news.headline: Reed chipped in nine points (3-6 FG, 3-5 FT), six rebounds, one assist and two steals in 22 minutes during Tuesday's 104-86 win over the Magic.
news.story: Reed continues to benefit from Jalen Duren's hamstring injury, which has opened additional frontcourt minutes. Reed's rebounding and defensive contributions provide short-term fantasy appeal in deeper leagues, but his role could shrink once Duren returns.

news.headline: Carter provided nine points (3-10 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 13 rebounds, three steals and two assists across 38 minutes during Tuesday's 104-86 loss to Detroit.
news.story: Carter narrowly missed out on a double-double, though his 13 rebounds led all players and matched his season-best mark. Tuesday's effort snapped a six-game stretch in which the big man recorded single-digit rebounds. On the year, Carter is averaging 12.5 points, 8.8 rebounds and 1.4 assists through 17 appearances.

news.headline: Carter amassed 15 points (5-11 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 3-3 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and one block in 32 minutes during Wednesday's 121-116 loss to Philadelphia.
news.story: Carter has scored in double figures in three consecutive games, averaging 12.3 points and 6.3 rebounds during that stretch. The veteran center has also connected on multiple three-pointers for the first time in November, providing an additional dimension to his offensive production. With Paolo Banchero (ankle) sidelined, Carter should continue seeing consistent minutes in Orlando's frontcourt, offering steady fantasy value in points and rebounds.

news.headline: Brown totaled 21 points (7-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal across 25 minutes during Friday's 124-100 loss to the Raptors.
news.story: Brown not only posted the best scoring output of his young career in the NBA, but he was extremely efficient for a player who has struggled with his shooting percentage in his first taste of NBA action. Brown should remain the Nets' starting point guard as long as he stays healthy. In three starts, he's averaging 14.7 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.0 steals per game while shooting 47 percent from three-point range.

news.headline: Brown finished Monday's 142-116 loss to the Timberwolves with 17 points (6-12 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, seven assists and one steal over 29 minutes.
news.story: Brown made his first career start with Nolan Traore (hamstring) sidelined. The rookie has scored at least 15 points in three straight games and could gain considerable fantasy value if he maintains a starting role, though turnovers remain a concern.

news.headline: Brown will start Monday's game against the Timberwolves, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
news.story: Brown has scored 15 and 18 points in his previous two showings, earning him the opportunity to join the starting five for the first time in his young NBA career. Coach Jordi Fernandez noted that Brown has been given the green light to log starter minutes, which would seemingly indicate that he'll sit around the 25-to-30-minute range Monday, though more clarity on his workload will be gleaned from how much he plays against the Timberwolves.

news.headline: Porter won't play Saturday against the Wizards as he's still in the process of getting up to speed on his conditioning.
news.story: Porter signed with the Magic on Nov. 25, so it's understandable that he'll need some time to get into playing shape. His next chance to play will come Sunday at Detroit on the second leg of a back-to-back set.

news.headline: Porter is signing a two-year contract with the Magic, Shams Charania of ESPN reports Wednesday.
news.story: Porter was waived by the Bucks following the preseason, though he's now set to provide backcourt depth for the Magic. He could challenge Jevon Carter for minutes behind Jalen Suggs right away. Over 38 regular-season appearances (36 starts) for Milwaukee last season, Porter averaged 17.4 points, 7.4 assists, 5.2 rebounds and 2.2 steals in 33.2 minutes per showing.

news.headline: Porter was waived by the Bucks on Monday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
news.story: Porter will need to search for an opportunity elsewhere after failing to secure a place on the regular-season roster. He averaged 17.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 7.4 assists and 2.2 steals in 38 regular-season appearances a year ago with Milwaukee.

news.headline: Brown (hamstring) is out for Friday's game against the Pacers.
news.story: Brown is set to undergo imaging of his hamstring, and all signs point to the star forward being on the verge of another spell on the sidelines. Brown has been out for just three games this season, but if he's forced to miss more time, Dean Wade could see an uptick in his playing time.

news.headline: Brown (hamstring) will receive imaging, and the Sixers will provide an update Thursday, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
news.story: Brown will get imaging on his troublesome left hamstring that he reaggravated in the second quarter of Wednesday's 111-104 win over Miami. He recently missed two games with the injury, and it sounds like he could be in jeopardy of another stint on the sidelines. While Brown is out, Dean Wade is the top candidate to join the starting unit, while Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Anfernee Simons are likely to see an increase in playing time off the bench.

news.story: Ware has logged at least 21 minutes in four straight games, providing a more stable role in Milwaukee's rotation. His rebounding and shot-blocking upside make him an intriguing fantasy option, though his playing time still limits his ceiling.

news.story: Edgecombe continues to contribute across multiple categories despite inconsistent scoring. He's averaged 17.3 points, 6.0 rebounds, 6.3 assists and 2.0 steals over his last three appearances, while his substantial playing time provides a strong fantasy foundation.

news.story: McDaniels scored a career-high 34 points in Monday's win over Brooklyn, and he narrowly missed that mark Wednesday. It's been a stellar 2026-27 campaign overall for the 26-year-old, who is now averaging 19.2 points, 6.4 rebounds and 3.8 assists, all career bests, along with 1.2 steals over 34.1 minutes in 19 regular-season appearances. With Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined and LaMelo Ball (ankle) exiting the meeting with the Thunder, McDaniels could continue to play at an All-Star level for the foreseeable future.

news.headline: Castle had 20 points (6-18 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 6-6 FT), six rebounds and nine assists across 34 minutes during Wednesday's 116-111 loss to the Trail Blazers.
news.story: The third-year guard just missed recording his fourth double-double of the season. news.story: Castle was forced into the spotlight Monday while the Spurs navigated without the services of De'Aaron Fox (shin), Dylan Harper (hip) and Victor Wembanyama (back), and he didn't disappoint. Castle looked sharp once again from downtown, where he's now hit at a clip of 54.2 percent from deep over his last four appearances. The 22-year-old also stepped up as a distributor and has secured a double-double in two of his last three showings.

news.story: Castle finished as the Spurs' second-leading scorer behind Victor Wembanyama, who led the way with 50 points, and Castle was particularly deadly from beyond the arc. Four of his five three-pointers came during a third-quarter stretch that helped San Antonio pull away for good. Castle's ability to contribute as both a scorer and facilitator gives him multiple paths to fantasy value, while efficient perimeter shooting adds another dimension to his offensive profile.

His layup with under two minutes left tied the game, though the Kings couldn't hold on. It was a big bounce-back after a rough shooting night against Phoenix on Wednesday.

news.story: Mara will miss a second consecutive contest due to a right shin contusion, with his next opportunity to play coming against Minnesota on Wednesday. With the rookie big man sidelined, Kenrich Williams and Micah Peavy are candidates for increased playing time.

news.headline: Nembhard put up 14 points (5-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, three assists and a steal in 25 minutes during Friday's 111-87 loss to the 76ers.
news.story: Nembhard extended his streak of double-digit scoring performances to seven, though his three assists tied a season low as the Pacers couldn't get much going offensively while shooting 34.9 percent from the floor. news.story: Nembhard continued to handle significant ball-handling responsibilities for Indiana, producing eight assists while contributing 16 points. However, his six turnovers were costly and diminished an otherwise useful fantasy performance. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) unavailable, Nembhard's opportunities to facilitate the offense remain substantial, making his assist production an important component of his fantasy value. He has also scored in double digits in five straight appearances, averaging 13.8 points, 2.8 rebounds and 8.8 assists per game in that stretch.

news.headline: Nembhard (hip) is available for Friday's game against the Cavaliers, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
news.story: Nembhard missed the last two games while dealing with a hip issue. After initially carrying a questionable designation, he is good to go for Friday's meeting with the Cavs. As a result, Quenton Jackson is expected to head back to the bench.

news.headline: Wiggins finished Friday's 87-86 win over Boston with 11 points (4-8 FG, 3-7 3Pt) and three steals.
news.story: Wiggins scored eight of his 11 points in the second quarter, and he finished fourth on the Hawks in scoring behind Jalen Johnson (24 points), Nickeil Alexander-Walker (20) and Luguentz Dort (14). news.story: Making his second start of the season, Wiggins scored 12 of his 19 points in the second half to finish as the Hawks' second-leading scorer behind Jalen Johnson (26). news.headline: Bridges contributed 12 points (5-8 FG, 2-3 3Pt), two rebounds, three assists and one steal across 28 minutes during Saturday's 97-96 victory over the Trail Blazers.
news.story: While Bridges' numbers from Saturday's game don't jump off the page, he came through when it mattered most for New York, drilling a buzzer-beating triple to save the day for the Knicks after they blew a 26-point lead. news.story: After carrying a questionable tag ahead of both parts of this back-to-back, Siakam is suiting up Monday despite dealing with a left hip injury. news.story: Jokic was his usual efficient self, leading Denver in scoring and assists. He capped the night by setting up an Aaron Gordon alley-oop in the final seconds. news.story: The Knicks are down Karl-Anthony Towns (illness) and OG Anunoby (calf), so Shamet's services will be required in the starting lineup. news.headline: Brown totaled 21 points (7-10 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-4 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal across 25 minutes during Friday's 124-100 loss to the Raptors.
news.story: Brown not only posted the best scoring output of his young career in the NBA, but he was extremely efficient for a player who has struggled with his shooting percentage in his first taste of NBA action. Brown should remain the Nets' starting point guard as long as he stays healthy. news.headline: Brown finished Monday's 142-116 loss to the Timberwolves with 17 points (6-12 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 1-1 FT), five rebounds, seven assists and one steal over 29 minutes.
news.story: Brown made his first career start with Nolan Traore (hamstring) sidelined. The rookie has scored at least 15 points in three straight games and could gain considerable fantasy value if he maintains a starting role, though turnovers remain a concern.

news.headline: Brown will start Monday's game against the Timberwolves, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
news.story: Brown has scored 15 and 18 points in his previous two showings, earning him the opportunity to join the starting five for the first time in his young NBA career. Coach Jordi Fernandez noted that Brown has been given the green light to log starter minutes, which would seemingly indicate that he'll sit around the 25-to-30-minute range Monday, though more clarity on his workload will be gleaned from how much he plays against the Timberwolves.

news.headline: Castle had 20 points (6-18 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 6-6 FT), six rebounds and nine assists across 34 minutes during Wednesday's 116-111 loss to the Trail Blazers.
news.story: The third-year guard just missed recording his fourth double-double of the season. news.story: Castle was forced into the spotlight Monday while the Spurs navigated without the services of De'Aaron Fox (shin), Dylan Harper (hip) and Victor Wembanyama (back), and he didn't disappoint. Castle looked sharp once again from downtown, where he's now hit at a clip of 54.2 percent from deep over his last four appearances. The 22-year-old also stepped up as a distributor and has secured a double-double in two of his last three showings.

news.headline: Castle posted 19 points (7-12 FG, 5-7 3Pt), three rebounds and six assists over 29 minutes during Saturday's 114-91 win over the Pelicans.
news.story: Castle finished as the Spurs' second-leading scorer behind Victor Wembanyama, who led the way with 50 points, and Castle was particularly deadly from beyond the arc. Four of his five three-pointers came during a third-quarter stretch that helped San Antonio pull away for good. Castle's ability to contribute as both a scorer and facilitator gives him multiple paths to fantasy value, while efficient perimeter shooting adds another dimension to his offensive profile.

news.story: Edgecombe continues to contribute across multiple categories despite inconsistent scoring. He's averaged 17.3 points, 6.0 rebounds, 6.3 assists and 2.0 steals over his last three appearances, while his substantial playing time provides a strong fantasy foundation.

news.headline: Wilson is undergoing surgery for a fractured right hand and will miss at least four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
news.story: The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey and Matas Buzelis offensively going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value for the next month or so.

news.headline: Wilson won't return to Wednesday's game against the Spurs due to a right hand injury. He'll finish with 15 points (5-7 FG, 2-2 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds and one steal in 15 minutes.
news.story: Wilson turned in an efficient performance en route to 15 points before exiting Wednesday's contest early in the third quarter. The rookie forward's status will be worth monitoring ahead of Friday's game against Atlanta. If he's forced to miss time, Leonard Miller, Patrick Williams and Noa Essengue would be candidates for increased minutes.

news.headline: Wilson exited to the locker room in the third quarter of Wednesday's game against San Antonio due to an apparent hand injury, K.C. Johnson of Chicago Sports Network reports.
news.story: Wilson was spotted holding his hand while heading back to the locker room. The rookie forward can be considered questionable to return until more information comes to light.

news.story: Duren has been dealing with a hamstring strain since October, and his return is not yet expected in immediate contests. The fact that he has practiced with the G League club is still a good sign as he makes progress in his recovery. Duren would be a reliable source of production once he's healthy, but until then, John Collins and Paul Reed may continue to absorb his responsibilities at center.

news.headline: Duren (hamstring) is being assigned to the Motor City Cruise on Wednesday for practice as he ramps up for a potential return, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports.
news.story: With Duren still out for Detroit but now progressing to a G League practice assignment, this marks a tangible step forward in his recovery from the right hamstring strain that has kept him sidelined since Oct. 23. The Pistons haven't provided a return timeline, but his return appears to be drawing closer as he increases his activity.

news.headline: Duren (hamstring) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Magic.
news.story: Duren hasn't played since Oct. 23 due to a right hamstring strain, though he's expected to be re-evaluated soon. Until the Pistons offer an update on the 23-year-old big man's progress, he can be considered week-to-week. Paul Reed will likely continue seeing increased minutes for as long as Duren is sidelined.

news.headline: Wiggins finished Friday's 87-86 win over Boston with 11 points (4-8 FG, 3-7 3Pt) and three steals.
news.story: Wiggins scored eight of his 11 points in the second quarter, and he finished fourth on the Hawks in scoring behind Jalen Johnson (24 points), Nickeil Alexander-Walker (20) and Luguentz Dort (14). Wiggins' three steals were a season high, and the sixth-year forward is averaging a career-best 13.8 points per game along with 3.4 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 1.0 steals and 2.8 threes over 25.5 minutes per contest.

news.story: Kingston Flemings (back) has been cleared to return to action, sending Wiggins back to the second unit. The 27-year-old forward has averaged 14.0 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 2.8 three-pointers in 25.4 minutes per contest across his last five outings off the bench.

news.story: Nembhard extended his streak of double-digit scoring performances to seven, though his three assists tied a season low as the Pacers couldn't get much going offensively while shooting 34.9 percent from the floor. He's valuable as a streaming option at center when he receives a fair share of playing time and offensive touches, but if that's not the case, his upside is fairly limited in other categories, especially the defensive ones.

Oklahoma City's injuries have opened more minutes for him, and he's taking advantage.

news.story: Bridges had his best game of the season, setting season highs in points and rebounds. His role has shrunk this year, but nights like this show he can still be a factor. With OG Anunoby (calf) sidelined, Bridges should keep getting extended minutes at the wing.

news.story: Jokic was his usual efficient self, leading Denver in scoring and assists. He capped the night by setting up an Aaron Gordon alley-oop in the final seconds. news.story: After carrying a questionable tag ahead of both parts of this back-to-back, Siakam is suiting up Monday despite dealing with a left hip injury. news.story: Siakam played through the issue Sunday, but the quick turnaround could prompt Indiana to exercise caution. With Tyrese Haliburton sidelined, Siakam's potential absence would leave a significant offensive void and create additional opportunities for the Pacers' remaining forwards.

news.headline: Siakam supplied 25 points (9-22 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-4 FT), six rebounds, one assist and two steals over 33 minutes during Sunday's 113-106 loss to the Knicks.
news.story: Siakam shouldered much of Indiana's scoring responsibility, leading the team in points and field-goal attempts while converting three shots from beyond the arc. news.story: Larsson bounced back from a four-point outing in his return from illness, matching his season high in scoring. news.headline: Larsson ended with four points (1-2 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal across 15 minutes during Wednesday's 137-130 victory over the Bucks.
news.story: Larsson returned to the starting lineup after missing three consecutive games due to an illness, but his playing time was significantly reduced. His minutes will be worth monitoring as he works his way back into Miami's rotation, though his limited offensive involvement makes him a risky fantasy option in standard leagues.

Jones has posted 10 or more points in five of his last six appearances and continues to add value as a facilitator despite his bench role.
